fields.Name: International Cheese Federation: Industry News and Market Updates
fields.Description: A collection of industry news articles from the International Cheese Federation, offering updates and analysis on fluctuating milk prices, tight margins, cheese demand, milk production trends, and the impact of federal policies and international trade disputes on the dairy and cheese markets for its members.

Yuri Lee 




 


Milk prices recover, margins stay tight 

 

Milk prices are climbing back after a rough 2018, and members processing their own supply say the recovery looks better on the board than on the ledger. 


Continue Reading

Mar 



 


 

 

Industry News 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Fewer cows, a steady case 

 

National milk cow numbers keep drifting down while cheese demand holds steady. We look at what a slow-growth spring means for members on both sides of the vat. 


Continue Reading

Mar 



 


 

 

Industry News 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Margins firm up, but keep an eye on the fall 

 

Milk prices are finally climbing out of a two-year trough, but an international trade dispute working its way through arbitration could reshape the cheese case before the year is out. 


Continue Reading

Yuri Lee 




 


A slower milk week, and what it means for you 

 

Federal market reporting for this week shows milk production growth still barely above flat. Here’s what that quiet number actually means for members buying, not just making, cheese. 


Continue Reading

Industry News 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Margins hold, and the cheese case doesn’t slow down 

 

A second federal safety-net payment landed this month, and specialty cheese kept outperforming the broader dairy case. Here’s what both numbers mean for members. 


Continue Reading

Yuri Lee 




 


Two markets, one cheese case 

 

Commodity cheese is drowning in surplus while our artisan members can’t make enough to fill orders. Both things are true at once, and the gap is where our members live.

Reading the market without the data 

 

With federal statistics only now catching back up after a five-week lapse, members are pricing January without the usual numbers. Here’s what we do know.
